name: Box and interval summary
reader_question: How do the centre, middle half and full range of a measure compare across groups?
relationship: Five-number summary per group on one shared axis: minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum.
use_when: A source reports five-number summaries rather than raw observations
Groups have enough observations (at least 5) for quartiles to mean something
avoid_when: Raw observations are few and available — use strip-plot
The shape of one distribution matters — use histogram
The audience is unlikely to read quartiles

data_contract.notes: Explicit shared axis containing every summary value
Unique group name and its observation count, shown on every row
Five stated numbers, ordered min ≤ q1 ≤ median ≤ q3 ≤ max

units: One unit and one shared axis across all rows.

editable: Whiskers, boxes, median lines, gridlines and labels are native shapes and text
not_data_bound: All five numbers per group are positioned from the fixture and are not data-bound; there is no embedded workbook, so editing a value means resizing the shapes and relabelling

table_alternative: A table of group, n, minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum.
variations: Strip-plot overlay when raw observations exist
limitations: Quartiles from small n are unstable; n is printed on every row
Boxes hide multimodality and cannot show individual outliers
Whiskers here are the stated minimum and maximum, not a statistical fence

excluded_alternatives.reason: Implies a symmetric confidence interval the five-number summary does not provide
Notches imply a significance test; none is supplied
